lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.units: css px (1 px = 0.2646 mm), letter 816x1056, from geometry.json and contrast.json
measurements.margins: The text boxes sit 82 px (21.7 mm) from the left and right edges but only 52 px (13.8 mm) from the bottom. That is an 8 mm difference against a 1 mm tolerance, so the margin check FAILS. The top is the bleeding field, so it is exempt. Actual glyph extents: left about 99 px (Dry-Hopped IPA), right about 104 px (Spirits prices), bottom about 56 px.
measurements.left_edges: Everything is centred. The text boxes share x (148 for cocktails; 82, 306 and 530 for the three columns), but the glyph left edges of the cocktail names spread from 268 (Old Fashioned description) and 322 (Old Fashioned name) to 349 (Margarita), about 76 px, so they have no shared left edge. The check FAILS as written. The centre axes hold: cocktails at 408, the three-up columns at 184, 408 and 632, and 408 is the page centre.
measurements.cross_column_rows: Row starts in the three-up row are staggered. Beer items sit at 743.2, 801.3 and 859.3; wine at 769.2, 827.3 and 916.3; spirits at 769.2, 806.4 and 874.6. The columns share no baselines and are offset by 26 px (one subhead step), so there is no shared baseline grid across columns.
measurements.price_column: There is no price column. Prices are one consistent inline style, 0.62 em after the name, integers with no $, tabular, at the same size as the names. Right-edge alignment does not apply.
measurements.price_pair_scan: Manhattan name right edge 440.7, price left edge 452.2: gap 11.5 px, which is 2.2% of the 520 px measure. Every row is about 2-6% of its column width, so no row exceeds 40%. PASS.
measurements.headers: The H2s are one style (DM Sans 600, 9.4 pt, tracked caps, indigo) and share y 714.7 across all three columns. H2 to first line is 28.5 px everywhere, H3 to item is 26.0 px everywhere and the item end to the next H3 is 20.0 px everywhere. Amber Lager to CIDER is 30 px. PASS.
measurements.item_spacing: The pitch is 58.1/58.0 px for two-line items and 37.2 px for spirits (one line). The gap between items is a constant 15 px. PASS.
measurements.dead_space: The columns end at 1004 (beer/cider), 959.4 (wine) and 896.8 (spirits): a spread of 107 px (28 mm). That leaves an empty block of about 224x107 px under Spirits and about 45 px under Wine, so the check FAILS. The 50 px plum band is also an empty full-width stripe with no job.
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: Minimum 6.6:1 (muted descriptions and subheads on flat paper). Names and prices 14.36:1, H2 13.23:1, wordmark 13.23:1 on flat indigo. There is no texture, so the worst pixel equals the flat ground. PASS.
measurements.type_sizes: Names and prices 13.9 pt, descriptions 9.75 pt, H2 9.4 pt, H3 11.25 pt italic. The H2s are smaller than the names they govern and differ from the ink mainly by hue (indigo #1E2147 vs ink #221C22), so the section heads nearly disappear at arm's length.
measurements.bleed: The proposal says the field bleeds 3 mm on the top, left and right. The geometry file only gives the trim box (x 0, w 816), so the bleed cannot be verified. All text is inside the safe inset.
measurements.accent_share: Accent is 27.4% of the whole page and 0.00% below the horizon, so the reading layer has no accent at all.
measurements.content_check: The 3 spirits have no description element; the proposal flags this as a gap. Cocktail descriptions name the spirit plus 2 or more ingredients. Descriptions such as 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward' and 'Sparkling' are too thin to support a choice.

top_problem: The boldest idea this design is missing is an art gesture that belongs to a Mexican cantina in Iowa. The horizon thesis becomes three full-width flat stripes above a centred wedding-invitation list. It reads as a letterhead banner, not art: nothing is cropped by the page edge, nothing leads the eye into the list, and the colour stops at the amber line. It fails the substitution test, because you could replace CANTINA with BISTRO or HOTEL and nothing would change. Next to ref-02 (panels 1-5: painterly agave cropped off the edge, a sun disc with a stair, a vertical brush wordmark, a floral rail, each with tight two-column lists and a short price hop), J has the restraint but not the idea. The centred lists add ragged edges, staggered rows across columns and a dead block under Spirits. This is clean, safe and forgettable.
remove: The plum middle band. It is a 50 px empty stripe that turns the horizon into a flag (indigo/plum/amber tricolour). One hard indigo-to-amber edge makes the horizon line more clearly and gives the space back to the reading layer.
fixes: Make the horizon a real art gesture, not a banner: for example, let one flat Iowa-field or adobe-step silhouette in the dusk inks break the horizon line and bleed off a side edge. Crop it so it points into COCKTAILS, keep text 6 mm clear of it, and verify with the image-substitution test.

Replace the centred stacks with flush-left short columns (a shared left edge per column, price a short hop after the name, as in ref-02) and lock the three-up row to one baseline grid, so that beer, wine and spirits items share y positions instead of staggering by 26 px.

Balance the columns and margins: set the bottom margin equal to the 21.7 mm sides (or declare the asymmetry), and redistribute the three-up content (for example, move Cider under Spirits) so the columns end within 1 baseline of each other and the 107 px dead block under Spirits disappears.

Bring the single accent below the horizon in exactly one place: set the H2 section heads in amber (checked to 4.5:1 on paper, or a darkened amber), not in near-ink indigo. The heads would then read as the accent, as in ref-02, rather than vanishing next to 13.9 pt names.

Give the reading layer something to choose by: replace the one-word descriptors ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling') with ingredient- or style-first lines from sourced data, and add a sourced line for the three spirits, so the page is not half names with nothing under them.

lens: Items and prices against build/draft_doc.json, ingredient names and how complete the descriptions are (meta.public_components respected), section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The menu is accurate but thin. All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly. The Manhattan correctly hides aromatic bitters, and no side-rail text or tagline states an item fact. But below the cocktails the descriptions shrink to single adjectives ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling'). No beer or cider has an ABV and no wine has a region. The three spirits (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) have no description at all and no missing_ingredients flag on the page. At a Mexican cantina, the agave pours are the least described items, sitting in the bottom-right column that ends 107 css px short of the other columns.
problems: Criterion 8: the spirits print no description and are not flagged. Blanco, Añejo and VSOP give type and age through the name only, with no brand, producer or pour size. The gap is listed in proposal.md as 'not blocking', but the scorecard requires missing_ingredients to be flagged and asked for, not quietly dropped.

Criterion 8: beer has no ABV (0 of 3), cider has no ABV, and wine has no region (0 of 3). The scorecard requires style + ABV for beer and grape + region for wine. None of this data is in the draft, so it must be flagged, not left blank.

Criterion 8/10: garnish appears only on the Manhattan (cocktail cherry). The Margarita, House Daiquiri and Old Fashioned show no garnish and have no flag, so the cocktail descriptions look complete when the data is not.

Criterion 10: the description voice breaks between the tiers. Cocktails get full ingredient lists with middots; beer, wine and cider get one- or two-word fragments ('Toasty', 'Sparkling', 'Dry sparkling'). Cutting the name echo left 'Amber Lager / Toasty' and 'Dry Cider / Sparkling' as stubs, not descriptions.

Criterion 5: one clear entry point (CANTINA, then COCKTAILS), but the three-up row has no set reading order (across or down?). Cider sits inside the Beer column, a move away from the draft order (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider). The column heights are 289 / 245 / 182 px, so the bottom right is empty. Centring every line (names, prices, descriptions) makes scanning a column of names and prices harder than a shared left edge would.

Criterion 5 (venue fit): for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Agave is the category guests expect most, yet it sits last and least developed; Mezcal and Reposado are also missing from the draft.

Criterion 3: prices are consistent (no $, whole numbers, tabular figures, set 0.62em after the name) and eye travel is short. But no item has a serve or pour label: Brut Rosé under 'Sparkling' has no glass/bottle label, spirits have no pour size, and beer has no size. Because each price moves with its centred name, prices do not line up in a scannable column.

Gates: every price (15, 15, 14, 16, 7, 8, 7, 12, 11, 13, 12, 16, 18, 8) matches the draft. No item was invented, changed or dropped; Aromatic Bitters is correctly hidden on the Manhattan. The only sub-line is '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa', which is a venue fact, not an item fact. Each price sits on its item's name line and each description sits directly under its name, so both gates pass.
fixes: Under Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP, print a sourced type/age line or an explicit missing_ingredients flag (brand, pour size), and send the request to the Coordinator so the spirits are not left undescribed.
Flag the missing ABV for all three beers and the cider, and the missing region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, as missing_ingredients requests. Print them once the facts are supplied.

Replace the stub descriptions with the full draft text, even if it echoes the name: 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Hop-forward draft IPA'. This keeps one voice with the cocktail tier.
Re-balance the three-up row: move Agave so it opens the lower tier or gets more weight (a venue-fit priority for a cantina), and even out the column heights to close the empty bottom-right.

Add serve labels where the data allows (glass for the By the Glass wines, 'pour' for spirits) and flag the missing garnish for the Margarita, House Daiquiri and Old Fashioned rather than implying the lists are complete.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient and label to build/draft_doc.json and to phg.menu_items / phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 212). Checked how descriptions and prices sit together in explore-J/preview-letter.png, including the menu_item_association gate.
top_problem: Each price is set in the same Fraunces 500 18.5 px as its item name, with no $ sign, no change in weight or colour, and only a 0.62em gap. In the spirits column the price reads as part of the name: 'Cognac VSOP 18', 'Añejo Tequila 16' and 'Blanco Tequila 12' look like 18-, 16- and 12-year age statements. That is a fact no source supports. On top of that, centred rows put every price at a different x position, so the guest cannot scan prices down a column.
problems: VERIFIED (sourced): Manhattan 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry' traces to draft_doc beta_manhattan components Rye Whiskey / Sweet Vermouth / Cocktail Cherry and to recipe_versions 9fb77eaa garnish 'Cocktail cherry'. Aromatic bitters are correctly left off because public_components aromatic-bitters=false. Margarita (f06abb74), House Daiquiri (14d45e57) and Brown Butter Old Fashioned (7095fd3d) ingredient lists match their draft components. Every price matches menu_items.menu_price (15/15/14/16/7/8/7/12/11/13/12/16/18/8). Accents on Añejo and Rosé match the source. No glass, garnish, ABV, region or brand is invented.

Garnish policy is inconsistent. Only the Manhattan prints its garnish. The sourced garnishes for the others are left off: Margarita 'Lime wheel' (rv f06abb74), Daiquiri 'Lime coin' (rv 14d45e57) and Old Fashioned 'Orange peel' (rv 7095fd3d). Readers will assume the other three drinks have no garnish.

Capitalisation is recased from the source ('Rye Whiskey' printed as 'Rye whiskey', 'Tequila Blanco' as 'Tequila blanco', 'Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon' as 'Brown butter-washed bourbon'). Sentence case is defensible, but the scorecard asks for the source's spelling and capitalisation, so this is noted.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe=false in draft_doc, yet it is printed under 'House Originals' with its full prep list. The printed words are covered by the draft desc 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.', so this is not an invented fact. The Coordinator should still confirm that house_recipe=false allows publishing the prep names.

Draft and database have drifted apart. phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b now includes 'Junmai Ginjo' ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which is missing from build/draft_doc.json (revision 3, synced 2026-09-23) and from the menu. This is not a gate fail in this lens because the brief names draft_doc.json as the source, but the Coordinator must resolve it before approval.

Description quality: the beer, wine and cider descriptions are cut down to fragments or taxonomy: 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'. The cocktails are bare ingredient lists with no appetite language, and the one sourced flavour line was dropped (Margarita 'Bright and citrus-forward.', menu_items 14555870). All three spirits have no description at all, which makes that column read as unfinished.

Venue fit: this is a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, yet apart from the word CANTINA nothing on the page is Mexican. The sub-line reads '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' and says nothing about the restaurant. The Margarita is second under Classics behind a Manhattan. Agave has two lines in the last column, at the same weight as the Cognac. There are no Spanish section heads and no tequila or mezcal emphasis. The dusk-horizon art is Iowa, not cantina. The same page would work for any hotel lobby bar.

No glass or bottle labels. 'Brut Rosé 13' sits under 'Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label ('By the Glass' covers only Malbec and Pinot Grigio). The spirits show no pour size. Neither the draft nor menu_items has a label for these prices, so they need a flag and a question, not a guess.

Layout: in the three-up row the Spirits column ends about 107 css px above Draft Beer/Cider (182 vs 289 px, geometry.json). Because the spirits have no descriptions, that corner is a dead block. Centred single-line descriptions are readable at 9.75 pt, and nothing is orphaned or crowded.
fixes: Set prices apart from names: use a lighter weight or the muted ink colour, a $ sign or a thin space plus middot, or a small-caps figure style. This stops 'Cognac VSOP 18' and 'Añejo Tequila 16' from reading as age statements (designer layout note).

Print the sourced garnish on all four cocktails (Lime wheel rv f06abb74, Lime coin rv 14d45e57, Orange peel rv 7095fd3d) or on none, and restore the Margarita's sourced flavour line 'Bright and citrus-forward' (menu_items 14555870).

Make the menu read as a Mexican cantina: lead Cocktails with the Margarita, give Agave more weight than Brandy, and use a correct Spanish kicker or heads (for example 'Bebidas', 'Tequila y Mezcal' only once mezcal exists in the data). Fix the sub-line so it states restaurant & cocktail bar.

Put the fuller draft descriptions back where they are more than a name echo ('Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Toasty amber lager'), and flag missing_ingredients (producer, region, ABV, pour size, glass/bottle for Brut Rosé) instead of printing one-word fragments or leaving spirits bare.
Resolve the Junmai Ginjo drift between phg.menu_items and draft_doc revision 3 before this direction is filed.
